title: Grateful Dead Live at Saenger Performing Arts Center on 1982-09-09
source: flac16/48kHz; Source Info: Dan Healy's Master Soundboard Cassettes (Sony TC-D5M/TDK MA-R90/Dolby B)> Frank Streeter's 1st generation 1/4 track Reels @ 3.75 ips (Sony TC770/Maxell UD35-90B) > Dat (16-bit/48k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony PCM-R500)> Tascam DA-3000 (wav 16-bit/48k)> Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac1648; the original version had a duplicate "Space" ("Drums > Space" were 1 track, followed by "Space" again)

ai_review.summary: Fair‑quality soundboard recording with noticeable pitch and balance problems, but a solid second set highlighted by a monster Wheel and strong Estimated Prophet.
ai_review.review: The patched SBD capture suffers from fast pitch playback, a brief dropout in Space and overall mix imbalance, making the audio only fair. Musically the show picks up after an uneven first set – Jerry muffs Mississippi Half‑Step and Althea is cut short – but the second set delivers a hot Estimated Prophet jam, a legendary Wheel performance and a tight Good Lovin' that justify the show's three‑star rating.

ai_rating.rationale: Review rates the show 3 stars overall; recording issues pull the technical score down while the second set’s strong performances raise the musical score, yielding an average‑plus rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pitch runs 2‑4% fast across most tracks, requiring correction; brief dropout at start of Space; overall balance needs adjustment; mix is acceptable but not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is uneven and ends abruptly with Althea cut short; second set recovers with strong tempos, a long jam into Eyes, and an especially memorable Wheel leading into the encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Muffs Mississippi Half-Step, adds extra parts on Franklin's Tower, flubs Feel Like a Stranger, drops solo in West L.A., relies on repeated phrasing during fast Samson, and takes rhythm duties after Althea.
band_member_comments.Bob: Frustrated by equipment problems, leaves the stage early during Althea, causing an abrupt set end.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland steps forward after Althea; no specific keyboard highlights noted beyond his presence.
